title: Unified disclosure policy and command display contract
objective: Derive a product-independent policy that decides when output is hidden, folded to one line, summarized, or fully displayed, then apply it to every command family in this project.

include: Decision inputs such as user intent, risk, outcome, novelty, duration, volume, repetition, interactivity, and accessibility
Information contracts for file, search, shell, web, MCP, task/team, plan/worktree, permission, and messaging commands
Default, running, success, warning, error, and user-expanded views
Data retention independent from visual disclosure
exclude: A single line-count threshold used as the entire policy

deliverables: A deterministic disclosure decision table with precedence rules
A command-family display matrix naming required and optional fields
Edge cases and anti-patterns that invalidate naive truncation
acceptance_criteria: Errors, approvals, destructive actions, and user-requested detail cannot be silently collapsed
Repeated low-value success events can be grouped without losing exact evidence
Screen-reader and narrow-terminal behavior are explicitly addressed
verification: Run the policy against representative success, failure, approval, long-output, and repeated-event examples

result.summary: Unified D0-D3 disclosure policy, priority rules, command-family contracts, accessibility constraints, and acceptance tests.
